subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Movement of substances (diffusion, osmosis, active transport)

questions.q: Which set of structures is found in BOTH animal and plant cells?
options: Nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane and mitochondria
Cell wall, chloroplasts and permanent vacuole
questions.explain: Nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane and mitochondria are common to both, whereas cell walls, chloroplasts and permanent vacuoles are only in plant cells.

questions.q: What does the nucleus of a cell contain and control?
options: Genetic material (DNA) and controls the cell's activities
Enzymes for respiration and controls energy release
questions.explain: The nucleus contains the genetic material (DNA) and controls the activities of the cell.

questions.q: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy for the cell.

questions.q: The cell wall of a plant cell is made mainly of which substance?
questions.explain: The plant cell wall is made of cellulose, which gives the cell strength and support.

questions.q: In which structure is the green pigment chlorophyll found?
questions.explain: Chlorophyll is contained in chloroplasts, where it absorbs light for photosynthesis.

questions.q: What is the function of ribosomes in a cell?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in the cell.

questions.q: Which three structures are present in a plant cell but absent from an animal cell?
options: Cell wall, chloroplasts and permanent vacuole
questions.explain: Plant cells additionally have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole.

questions.q: What is the main role of the permanent vacuole in a plant cell?
options: It is filled with cell sap and helps keep the cell firm (turgid)
It controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explain: The permanent vacuole is filled with cell sap and helps support the cell by keeping it turgid.

questions.q: Which structure controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell?
questions.explain: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell as it is partially permeable.

questions.q: Which structure is absent from a mature red blood cell?
questions.explain: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus, giving more room for haemoglobin to carry oxygen.

questions.q: A root hair cell has a long, thin extension. How does this adapt it to its function?
options: It gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions
It allows the cell to carry out photosynthesis
It helps the cell swim towards the roots
It lets the cell carry oxygen efficiently
questions.explain: The long extension increases the surface area, speeding up absorption of water and mineral ions from the soil.

questions.q: Why does a sperm cell contain many mitochondria?
options: To provide energy for the tail to move so the cell can swim
To store genetic information for fertilisation
To carry out photosynthesis on its journey
questions.explain: Many mitochondria release the energy needed for the tail to beat and propel the sperm towards the egg.

questions.q: A leaf cell is packed with many chloroplasts and lies near the upper surface of the leaf. Which specialised cell is this?
questions.explain: Palisade mesophyll cells near the top of the leaf contain many chloroplasts to maximise photosynthesis.

questions.q: How is a red blood cell adapted to carry as much oxygen as possible?
options: It is biconcave and packed with haemoglobin, with no nucleus
It has a long tail and many mitochondria
It has many chloroplasts and a large vacuole
It has cilia to sweep oxygen along
questions.explain: The biconcave shape gives a large surface area and the lack of a nucleus leaves more room for oxygen-carrying haemoglobin.

questions.q: Diffusion is best described as the net movement of particles from an area of...
options: High water potential to low water potential only
One partially permeable membrane to another
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient, from high to low concentration.

questions.q: Osmosis is the movement of which substance across a partially permeable membrane?
questions.explain: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: In osmosis, in which direction does water move?
options: From a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution
From a concentrated solution to a more dilute solution
From low water potential to high water potential
questions.explain: Water moves by osmosis from a dilute solution (high water potential) to a more concentrated solution (low water potential).

questions.q: Active transport differs from diffusion because it...
options: Requires energy from respiration and moves substances against the concentration gradient
Only moves water across a partially permeable membrane
Is a passive process needing no energy
Moves particles from high to low concentration
questions.explain: Active transport uses energy released by respiration to move substances against (up) the concentration gradient.

questions.q: Root hair cells absorb mineral ions from the soil even when the ion concentration is higher inside the cell than in the soil. Which process is this?
questions.explain: Absorbing ions against the concentration gradient requires energy, so it is active transport.

questions.q: A piece of potato is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. What happens to its mass and why?
options: It loses mass because water leaves the cells by osmosis
It gains mass because water enters the cells by osmosis
It gains mass because sugar enters by diffusion
Its mass stays the same because no water moves
questions.explain: The sugar solution is more concentrated than the potato cells, so water moves out by osmosis and the mass falls.

questions.q: A red blood cell is placed in pure water. What is most likely to happen?
options: Water enters by osmosis and the cell swells and may burst
Water leaves by osmosis and the cell shrinks
Salt diffuses in and the cell stays the same
Nothing happens because cells cannot take in water
questions.explain: Pure water has a higher water potential, so water enters the cell by osmosis; without a cell wall the cell may burst.

questions.q: Which change would INCREASE the rate of diffusion of a gas into a cell?
options: Decreasing the surface area of the membrane
Increasing the distance the gas must travel
questions.explain: A higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, so they move faster and diffusion is quicker.
